behavioral_effects: None stated. An empty list is a claim that nothing observably changes.
compatibility_impact: The chat-frontend invariant held: the WebSocket origin must be in connect-src, and the build-time derivation guarantees CSP and client fall back in step (client constants.ts defaults to ws://localhost:8100, compose/Dockerfile bake the same default). A production image built without NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL and served on a non-localhost domain would have a broken chat WS regardless of CSP - unchanged from before. Browser REST, i18n routing, and SSG page rendering verified unchanged in the production build.
reason: Security finding: the frontend CSP permits both unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval in every environment; unsafe-eval is only needed by dev tooling, and connect-src allows ws: and localhost origins that have no place in a production policy. Full unsafe-inline removal needs the nonce architecture and is recorded as the follow-up
rollback: git revert restores the permissive single CSP; reopens the unsafe-eval and open connect-src finding.
security_impact: Production frontend CSP no longer permits unsafe-eval, and connect-src no longer allows arbitrary ws:, wss:, or localhost origins: it names exactly self plus the WebSocket origin derived at build time from NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL (which the Dockerfile always bakes), falling back to wss: only when the variable is absent. Dev builds keep the permissive policy for HMR. unsafe-inline for scripts remains: Next hydration requires it without the per-request nonce architecture, which forces dynamic rendering on every route and is recorded as the follow-up path. Verified in a production build: landing, login, full login flow, and dashboard render with zero CSP violations, and the chat WebSocket origin is admitted (construction previously threw SecurityError under the tightened policy until the origin derivation landed).
summary: Drop unsafe-eval from the production frontend CSP and stop allowing plaintext websockets and localhost connects in production
